title: 1:1 prep - Avery Brooks & Casey Nguyen
content:
Context: monthly 1:1 with Casey (IC, infra team). Focus this month = unblock rollout automation work, career check-in (IC -> tech lead readiness), and sync on support rotation burnout impact. Quick notes to self + agenda and proposed actions.

TL;DR for meeting:
- Status on rollout automation (ETA + remaining risks)
- One concrete blocker: flaky canary tests causing delays
- Career convo: interest in stepping into TL responsibilities in next 6 months; wants mentor + visible project
- Well-being: support rotation impacting focus; propose changes to rotation/backup

Agenda (30 min)
1) Quick personal check-in (3-4 min) - mood, energy, context (support rotation)
2) Rollout automation status (8-10 min)
   - What shipped since last 1:1
   - Remaining risks (canary flakiness, infra quota)
   - Ask: what do you need from me (time, PR review, stakeholder escalation)?
3) Career trajectory (8 min)
   - Casey wants to prep for TL: gaps = cross-team ownership exposure, stakeholder comms, design docs
   - Suggest 2-3 stretch opportunities: lead the next infra stability postmortem action plan; own the next cross-team rollout schedule
4) Well-being / support rotation (5 min)
   - Impact on deep work: quantify (hours lost/week?) and propose mitigations
5) Actions & follow-ups (2-3 min)

Prep notes / facts to reference:
- Rollout automation PRs: PR#2567 (partially reviewed), PR#2591 (tests failing on canary) - linked in GH:pr/2567
- Canary failures: flakiness spikes on Tuesdays (incidence ~ 40% last 3 runs). Root cause suspected test ordering + race in health-checker.
- SLA for Dedicated customers next quarter: need rollout stability >= 99.5% during migrations (context for prioritization).
- Casey current support rotation: 1 week oncall every 5 weeks; reports ~6-8 hours/day of interruptions on oncall days (from their notes) - ask them to quantify this during convo.

Questions to ask Casey:
- How confident are you in the rollout automation timeline? (1-5)
- What would 'ready for TL' look like for you in 6 months? 3 concrete milestones?
- Which parts of cross-team comms make you most uncomfortable? (planning meetings, async updates, stakeholder follow-ups)
- If we change support rotation, which option helps you most: fewer rotations, named backup per rotation, or protected deep-work days?

Potential manager commitments (what I can offer)
- Blocker escalation: escalate flaky canary tests to SRE lead + request extra CI quota for a week to repro reliably (I will follow-up by EOD if Casey ok).
- Assign Casey to lead the postmortem action plan for last month's outage (small project, cross-team). This gives exposure and a deliverable for TL candidacy.
- Set up monthly 1-1 mentoring slot (30 min) focused on design/PR reviews and stakeholder comms practice.
- Adjust support rotation trial: propose 6-week pilot with a dedicated backup for Casey; evaluate after 2 cycles.

Draft action items (post-meeting)
- Casey: run through flaky test reproducer on staging and post initial findings in GH issue PLT-4321 by 2026-03-03 (owner: Casey).
- Me (Avery): escalate PLT-4321 to SRE lead + request CI quota bump; send note to SRE by 2026-02-28 (owner: Avery).
- Me: nominate Casey to own the outage postmortem action plan and block 0.5 days/week for the next 3 weeks to lead it (start 2026-03-01).
- Me: schedule monthly mentoring blocks and assign first topic = "writing design docs for cross-team projects" (calendar invite sent by 2026-03-02).
- People Ops / rotation change: draft pilot proposal and run by Casey + oncall team; aim to trial starting 2026-03-15 (owner: Avery to coordinate).

Follow-ups to track (notes to self)
- Check progress on PR#2567 review; if stalled, offer to review or reassign reviewers.
- Watch for week-after-next canary run spike; if flakiness persists escalate earlier.
- Gather 2 examples of TL-like responsibilities Casey can take on (design lead, cross-team rollouts) and present in next 1:1.

Risks / unknowns:
- If canary flakiness needs deeper infra changes, timeline could slip >6 weeks. Need contingency: temp manual gating or additional test isolation.
- People Ops approval timeline for rotation pilot uncertain; have fallback (reduce oncall frequency for Casey for one quarter).

Notes to self (conversation style reminders):
- Start with empathy on burnout; don't immediately jump to process fixes.
- Reinforce that stepping into TL is a mutual growth plan; set clear measurable milestones.
- Ask Casey for 1 ask of me right now (what help do you need this week?).

Final: leave 2-3 min at end to confirm actions, owners, and dates. Quick ping in Slack after 1:1 with summary and links to PR/issue.

Previous 1:1 quick history:
- 2026-01-15: discussed PR review cadence, Casey asked for more async reviews
- 2026-01-29: agreed to start rotation trial conversation
- 2026-02-12: follow-up on automation alpha; tests were still flaky

End.
